name: Alinma Bank
legal_name: Alinma Bank (a Saudi Joint Stock Company)
founded: 2006 (Royal Decree No. M/15 dated 28 March 2006; CR 1010250808 dated 26 May 2008; listed on Tadawul 2008)
ownership_summary: Widely held Tadawul-listed bank. The Public Investment Fund is the only shareholder disclosed above 5%, holding 250,000,000 shares (10%) at both the start and end of 2025 (AR 2025). The bank was founded in 2006 with PIF, the Public Pension Agency and GOSI each holding 10% (IR site). Foreign ownership was 13.7% at 30 Jun 2026 (2Q26 investor presentation). Share capital rose to SAR 30bn through a 1-for-5 bonus issue approved by the EGM on 21 Apr 2026.
government_link: Yes. The Public Investment Fund holds 10% (31 Dec 2025, S5). The bank was founded in 2006 with PIF, the Public Pension Agency and GOSI as 10% founding shareholders each (S22). The Vice Chairman is a PIF executive (S2, S5).
group_structure: Parent bank with 100%-owned subsidiaries: Alinma Capital Company (CMA-licensed asset management, custody, advisory, underwriting and brokerage; profiled separately as sa-alinma-capital), Al-Tanweer Real Estate Company, Saudi Fintech Company (AlinmaPay), Esnad Company (outsourced staff), Alinma SPV Ltd (Cayman; derivatives and repo), TechStrike Company (technology services, est. Feb 2025) and Ersal Financial Remittance Company. The bank also consolidates Alinma Sukuk ETF (97.8%), Alinma Digital Fund (100%; fintech/payments private equity) and Alinma 8th Opportunities Real Estate Fund (100%) at 30 Jun 2026 (S3 note 1). Double counting: Alinma Capital's assets, revenue and AUM are consolidated in the bank's figures and its 'Investment and brokerage' segment. Do not add sa-alinma-capital metrics to this record.

footprint: Saudi Arabia only. 130 branches at 30 Jun 2026 (121 at 30 Jun 2025) (S3 note 1). 1,408 ATMs and 188,692 POS terminals at end-2025 (S5). 3 dedicated Private Banking centres in Riyadh (Lumiere Center), Jeddah (King Road Tower) and Al Khobar (S5, S9).
customer_segments: Retail (mass; youth through the 'iz' digital app; expats, with the Expats Affluent Banking package launched 2025), affluent tiers (alinma Gold, Platinum, Diamond), Private Banking (HNW), SME, corporate and institutional (S5, S9-S12).
business_lines: Four reportable segments (S3 note 12): Retail banking; Corporate banking (corporate, SME, institutional); Treasury; Investment and brokerage, run through Alinma Capital (asset management, brokerage, custody, advisory, investment banking). Investment and brokerage made up SAR 609.6m of SAR 6,138.1m total operating income in H1 2026 (about 10%). Private Banking Group sits within the bank. Other activities: digital payments and fintech (Saudi Fintech Company/AlinmaPay, Banking-as-a-Service), remittances (Ersal), bancassurance. All products are Shariah-compliant.

capabilities.wealth_summary: alinma is a fully Shariah-compliant Saudi bank. Its asset management, brokerage, custody and advisory sit in the 100%-owned Alinma Capital (renamed from Alinma Investment in Feb 2025), whose AUM was SAR 129.7bn at 30 Jun 2026 (+39% YoY). The bank describes it as the 3rd-largest asset manager in KSA by AUM at Q1 2026. The Private Banking Group runs three dedicated centres (Riyadh, Jeddah, Al Khobar) and grew its client base 26% and deposits 32% in 2025. Below it sit the published affluent tiers alinma Gold, Platinum and Diamond, with current-account entry deposits of SAR 75,000, 250,000 and 800,000. In 2025 the bank launched a digital wealth management platform in the alinma app with mutual fund subscriptions, and an Investor Financing programme for private clients investing in Saudi equities. Under Strategy 2030 (execution from 2026), Private Banking plans an 'open-architecture wealth ecosystem in partnership with global asset managers', an AI-powered wealth-advisory companion and a proposition for next-generation wealth holders. Alinma Capital's 2030 plan adds partnerships with global asset managers to co-develop funds, a top-tier wealth advisory team and a new engagement-led app.

private_banking.detail: Private Banking Group with 3 dedicated centres in Riyadh, Jeddah and Al Khobar and a dedicated-RM model. 2025: client base +26%, deposits +32%; since end-2022, clients +90%, deposits +47%, financing +135%. Offering per the alinma Private page: wealth management services, structured products, advanced FX solutions, 'direct investment with fixed returns at special prices', discounts on alinma capital products, Visa Infinite cards and concierge. 2025 launches: Investor Financing (structured financing for investing in Saudi equities); access to private equity via alinma capital; early-stage real estate project access and raw-land investments. 2030 goals: be 'the Islamic private bank of choice in Saudi Arabia'; open-architecture ecosystem with global asset managers; next-generation wealth proposition; AI-powered wealth-advisory companion; 'red carpet services' with strategic partners.

asset_management.detail: Through Alinma Capital (100%): AUM SAR 129.7bn at 30 Jun 2026 and SAR 104,607m at 31 Dec 2025. 72 funds at end-2025, including public equity, money market, Sukuk ETF, REIT, endowment, real estate and private equity funds. Alternatives AUM exceeded SAR 84bn at end-2025. Fund management fees are 50% of the bank's fees from banking services (H1 2026). See sa-alinma-capital.

brokerage.detail: Through Alinma Capital: Saudi market (Tadawul) plus GCC, Egypt, US, European and Asian markets via 'Alinma Capital Platform' (local) and 'Alinma Capital Global Platform'; web, app and phone channels; Murabaha margin facilities. Brokerage trading value SAR 32.4bn in H1 2026 (-4% YoY); brokerage trading income SAR 59.0m (-20% YoY). Brokerage is 8% of the bank's fee income.

digital_investing.detail: Bank app: Nama investment product (bank-managed Shariah investment pool) subscribe and track. In 2025 the bank also launched a 'digital wealth management platform with seamless mutual fund subscriptions' (AR 2025). Equities, IPOs, Sukuk orders and mutual fund subscription/redemption run in the separate Alinma Capital app and web platform; international trading via Alinma Capital Global. No in-app model portfolios, alternatives or international equities found in the bank app.

advisory.detail: RM-led advisory in Private Banking ('expertise-driven advisory with a Relationship Manager-led coverage approach'). Alinma Capital holds a CMA advising licence and offers investment management advisory based on an Investment Policy Statement. Strategy 2030 plans 'a top-tier wealth advisory team' at Alinma Capital.

discretionary.detail: Alinma Capital private investment portfolios / mandates (discretionary portfolio management). AUM about SAR 15bn at end-2025 per Alinma Capital AR; see sa-alinma-capital.

model_portfolios_robo.detail: No client-facing robo-advisor or model-portfolio product found in the bank app. Alinma Capital launched 'Nasih', an investment-allocation tool based on client data and risk profile, in 2025 (Alinma Capital AR; see sa-alinma-capital). It is unclear whether clients use it directly. Strategy 2030 plans an 'AI-powered wealth companion' and 'AI-powered app companions'.

funds_platform.detail: In-house funds (Alinma Capital) are distributed through the bank app's 2025 wealth management platform and the Alinma Capital app. No third-party fund shelf or fund-platform provider found.

structured_products.detail: 'Structured products and advanced foreign exchange solutions' are listed for alinma Private clients. No product details or issuers published.

private_markets.detail: Alinma Capital alternatives (real estate and private equity funds; alternatives AUM above SAR 84bn at end-2025). A new private fund with SAR 447mn AUM was launched in 2Q 2026. Private Banking gives clients access to private equity with alinma capital and to early-stage real estate projects. The bank consolidates Alinma Digital Fund (fintech PE) and Alinma 8th Opportunities Real Estate Fund.

islamic_wealth.detail: The whole franchise is Shariah-compliant under a Shariah Committee: Shariah funds, Alinma Sukuk ETF (Saudi government sukuk), Murabaha/Mudaraba customers' time investments, Nama investment pool.

partners.what: API marketplace platform on IBM Cloud Pak for Integration, IBM API Connect, Red Hat OpenShift on IBM Cloud and IBM DataPower. IBM's release calls IBM a technology partner; it does not describe a systems-integrator role.
Supplies funds, brokerage, custody and private-market products to bank clients; Private Banking collaborates on PE and real estate access

initiatives.what: Investment arm renamed from Alinma Investment to Alinma Capital (CMA notice)
Launched API marketplace platform built on IBM hybrid cloud and integration software (Banking-as-a-Service and open banking)
Launched a digital wealth management platform with mutual fund subscriptions in the alinma app; completed the 2021–2025 Digital Strategy and began the 2026–2030 Digital Strategy
Private Banking launched the Investor Financing programme (financing to invest in Saudi equities) and widened PE and real estate access with alinma capital

Fintech investments: Lean Technologies (open banking), Ejari, NearPay, Amwal Tech, Wadaie (deposit aggregation), Qashio, and VC funds Oryx, Sukna and SEEDRA. Cooperation agreements with Savvy Group, Walaplus, jisr and Future Work.

Strategy 2030 update (2Q26 presentation). Private Banking pillar: 'Set up market differentiating value propositions and service models for Private Banking clients' and 'Offer world-class global and exclusive local investments opportunities'. Alinma Capital pillar: partner with global AMs to co-develop funds, set up a top-tier wealth advisory team, launch a new app, AI-powered wealth companion. 9 of 13 Alinma Capital initiatives started.

Q2-26 call: CEO said the bank wants to 'build more strategic partnerships with global asset management to develop the region-specific investment opportunity for our customers' and to 'develop GenAI and AI-powered app companions'

opportunities: Private Banking 2030 plan: 'build an open-architecture wealth ecosystem in partnership with global asset managers, giving Private Banking clients early or exclusive access to high-quality onshore and offshore investment products' (S5 pp.100-103)
Private Banking 2030 plan includes an 'AI-powered wealth-advisory companion' and a proposition for next-generation wealth holders (S5 pp.100-103)

Alinma Capital 2030 focus areas: 'Forge partnerships with global AMs to co-develop funds', 'Set up a top-tier wealth advisory team', 'Launch cutting-edge app with engagement features and modules', 'Enhance CX with AI-powered wealth companion and personalization' (S6 slide 18)
CEO on 27 Jul 2026 call: plans 'more strategic partnerships with global asset management' and 'GenAI and AI-powered app companions' (S7)
The bank app's wealth offer is limited to mutual fund subscriptions (2025 platform) and the Nama pool. No model portfolios, international or alternatives access found in the bank app (S5, S14)
Brokerage is under pressure: H1 2026 brokerage trading income -20% YoY and trading value -4% YoY, while AUM grew 39% (S6 slide 47)
barriers: Islamic-only bank: every product must be Shariah-compliant and approved by its Shariah Committee (S3 note 1)
Investment licences sit in Alinma Capital (CMA licence 37-09134), so any investment-product contract would likely be with the subsidiary, not the bank (S3 note 1)
Large proprietary alternatives franchise (alternatives AUM above SAR 84bn) and in-house fund range compete with third-party private-markets shelves (S6; sa-alinma-capital)
Alinma Capital already runs its own trading apps and a global trading platform, and built the 'Nasih' allocation tool in-house in 2025 (see sa-alinma-capital)
incumbent_vendors: IBM: API platform (Cloud Pak for Integration, API Connect, Red Hat OpenShift on IBM Cloud, DataPower), live Feb 2025 (S15)

Global Trading Network (GTN): Alinma Capital's global trading login is hosted on a globaltradingnetwork.com subdomain and its Android app ID is com.gtn.alin. Inferred from official links, not announced (see sa-alinma-capital)
T24 core system at Alinma Capital, named in Alinma Capital AR 2025 (see sa-alinma-capital)

discrepancies.detail: Bank FY2025 FS note 38 gives Alinma Capital AUM of SAR 93,650m for 2024. Alinma Capital's own FY2025 FS note 22.1 gives SAR 90,103m. Both give SAR 104,607m for 2025.
discrepancies.resolution: Only the 2025 and 30 Jun 2026 figures are recorded, and these agree. Comparative difference unresolved; possibly a scope difference.

discrepancies.detail: AR 2025 executive management lists Abdullah Jamaan AlZahrani as Chief Treasury Officer. The 2Q26 presentation (Jul 2026) and the official executive page (checked 12 Oct 2026) list Mhana/Mahanna Abdulrahman Abaalkhail/Abalkhail.
discrepancies.resolution: Used the official page (most recent). No change announcement found. Name spelling follows the official page.

discrepancies.detail: AR 2025 lists Fahad Abdulaziz AlMohaimeed as Chief Strategy and Sustainability Officer. He is not on the official executive page or the 2Q26 management slide.
discrepancies.resolution: Not recorded as current; status unresolved.

discrepancies.detail: AR 2025 reports 6.5 Mn customers at 31 Dec 2025. The 2Q26 presentation reports 6.3 Mn 'Active Customers'.
discrepancies.resolution: Different definitions (total vs active). Both recorded with labels; not a decline.

discrepancies.detail: Internal notes said IBM was a systems integrator at Alinma. IBM's Feb 2025 release describes IBM as the technology/software provider for an API platform and mentions no consulting or integration services.
discrepancies.resolution: Recorded IBM as API/integration platform technology provider. Systems-integrator role not verified.

discrepancies.detail: The official board page describes Saad AlKroud as 'Current Chief of staff at the Public Investment Fund'; AR 2025 lists Chief of Staff among previous positions and gives 'Head of Local Real Estate Investment Division, Public Investment Fund (2025 – Present)'.
discrepancies.resolution: Used the AR 2025 wording (newer, tier 1); board page appears not to have been updated.

discrepancies.field: Chief Retail Banking Officer — earlier alinma role
discrepancies.detail: Official page: 'Assistant General Manager, Eastern Region' and 'General Manager of Branch Banking'; AR 2025: 'Regional Manager, Eastern Region' and 'Branch Manager', without the GM Branch Banking step.
discrepancies.resolution: Both versions recorded in previous_roles with attribution. Minor.

discrepancies.detail: Official executive page and AR 2025 give only 'Deputy Chief Executive Officer'; the Jan 2023 release says he continues to head the Retail & Digital Banking Executive Group, and on the 27 Jul 2026 call he was introduced as deputy CEO covering retail, digital and private.
discrepancies.resolution: Title recorded as on the official page; coverage kept in business_unit, functions and notes.

Head of Private Banking / wealth not named in any official source. The Deputy CEO covers retail, digital and private. Find the Private Banking Group head (LinkedIn/news).
Which funds (in-house only, or third-party) are on the bank app's 2025 wealth management platform: not documented publicly.
Alinma Private eligibility thresholds not published.
Lead not verified: Dell Technologies MoU on data centre/AI/cloud (seen only in a search result from a tech-news aggregator).

ALGadi; LinkedIn says since Mar 2025) and CIO (Yasser AlOufi; IBM release Feb 2025) remain absent from the official executive page (EN/AR), the AR 2025 executive section and the 2Q26 management slide; EN/AR role-based searches found no official announcement. Unverified leads seen in search results only (not opened, not cited): an aggregator naming Dr. Emad Al-Suhaibani as EVP & Chief Digital Officer in early 2024, and the bank's 4Q2021 investor presentation listing Sami Al Rowaithey as Chief Digitalization Officer. Both statuses kept at 'Requires verification'.

Head of Private Banking still unnamed: EN/AR role-based searches (2026-10-12) found only a Sep 2024 job posting for a private-banking relationship manager; the Deputy CEO covers retail, digital and private (Q2-26 call).
